title: Bunkie
subtitle: Finding safe, compatible roommates and shared housing in Nigeria
overview: Bunkie is a roommate and housing discovery app that helps people in Nigeria find compatible roommates and trustworthy shared accommodation with less stress, lower cost and more confidence. The product combines roommate matching, housing listings, identity verification, in-app messaging and booking into one mobile-first experience.
problem: Finding a roommate or shared home in Nigeria has no dedicated, structured platform. People post on Twitter, Facebook and WhatsApp groups, ask friends and family, or approach random landlords. These routes are scattered, slow and often unsafe: there is no central place, no trust layer, no structured matching, and too much money is lost to inspection fees, transport and fake listings.
solution: Bunkie gives people one safe, structured place to find a roommate or a shared home. Compatibility questions replace guesswork, ID verification replaces blind trust, and in-app messaging and booking keep the whole journey in one place, without agent fees.

features.title: Onboarding & Lifestyle Questionnaire
features.description: Email, Google and Apple sign-up lead into a profile and a short lifestyle questionnaire covering schedule, cleanliness, noise, pets, smoking, guests, religion, gender preference and budget.

features.title: Profile & ID Verification
features.description: Profiles carry the compatibility information roommates need, with a verified badge once government ID and selfie checks are complete.

features.title: Roommate & Housing Discovery
features.description: Search rooms or roommates, filter by price, location, room type and lifestyle, and move between ranked matches and shared-housing listings.

features.title: Messaging & Booking Requests
features.description: Chat unlocks on a mutual match, with report and block tools, while booking requests let a seeker express interest and a lister accept or decline.

features.title: Listing Creation & Management
features.description: Listers post a room in a guided flow, manage availability and publish, unpublish, mark as taken or extend a listing.

features.title: Design System & Prototype
features.description: A shared component library and interactive Figma prototype connect onboarding, verification, discovery, listing and booking before handoff.

architecture.title: Three journeys, one connected product
architecture.description: The experience is organised around three journeys: onboarding and compatibility, roommate and housing discovery, and the handoff from interest to chat. A shared design system and persistent bottom navigation keep the flows connected.

paragraphs: Bunkie is a roommate and housing discovery app that helps people in Nigeria find compatible roommates and trustworthy shared accommodation with less stress, lower cost and more confidence.

This was an 8-week project by a cross-functional team of UX designers, UI designers, brand designers and product managers. Our job was to research, design and document Bunkie to a standard a development team could pick up and build from.

paragraphs: Finding a roommate or shared home in Nigeria has no dedicated, structured platform. People post on Twitter, Facebook and WhatsApp groups, ask friends and family, or approach random landlords. These routes are scattered, slow and often unsafe.

cards.title: No central place
cards.body: Listings are spread across social media with no consistency, so search starts from scratch every time.

cards.title: No trust layer
cards.body: There is no easy way to verify that a person, landlord or listing is real, so scams are common.

cards.title: Poor matching
cards.body: People with a spare room and people looking for one have no structured way to find each other.

cards.title: Wasted money
cards.body: People pay inspection fees, transport costs and sometimes deposits for apartments that turn out to be fake or misrepresented.

callout.label: Design challenge
callout.text: How might we help people find a verified, compatible roommate and an affordable home without relying on expensive agents or risky social media posts?

sections.title: Who We Designed For
sections.intro: We started with three assumed user groups and refined them through research.

cards.title: Students
cards.body: Living away from home for the first time, on a tight budget, wanting affordable housing near campus.

cards.title: Young professionals and relocators
cards.body: New to a city, with no network to rely on for referrals and a short window to find somewhere safe.

cards.title: Existing tenants and homeowners
cards.body: People with a room or apartment who need a reliable person to share it with.

blocks.heading: Research narrowed these into three personas

personas.name: Amara
personas.summary: Moving from Ibadan to Lagos. She wants a safe, affordable room near work, but she knows nobody, fears scams and feels overwhelmed by WhatsApp group listings.
personas.quote: I just want to know the person I'm moving in with is normal and we won't clash.

personas.name: Tunde
personas.summary: Needs a room within budget and a study-focused roommate. Listings are overpriced or require guarantors, and roommates found on social media feel risky.
personas.quote: I need somewhere quiet, close to school, and someone who won't throw parties every night.

personas.name: Chisom
personas.summary: Based in Abuja and wants a quiet, responsible flatmate for her two-bedroom apartment. Vetting strangers is stressful after bad tenant experiences.
personas.quote: I don't want to post on Facebook again. I need a platform that actually vets people.

callout.label: The common thread
callout.text: Every persona was making a high-trust decision with low-trust tools.

paragraphs: We ran a UX survey with prospective users across Lagos, Ilorin, Bauchi and Port Harcourt. Respondents were NYSC members, students and young professionals, mostly aged 18 to 35, living with family, with roommates or in temporary accommodation.
The survey was paired with interviews and affinity mapping to separate recurring frustrations from one-off complaints.

stats.label: Had searched before
stats.description: Respondents who had previously looked for shared accommodation or a roommate

stats.label: Search timeline
stats.description: Most respondents took more than a month to secure their current place

stats.label: Age range
stats.description: Students, NYSC members and young professionals

blocks.heading: What we found
items: Almost everyone had searched before. Most had used agents.
Agents are the norm, and the main frustration. High agent and inspection fees were the top complaint, validating the idea of cutting agents out of the search.
Search takes too long. Most respondents took more than a month to secure their current place.
Scams are a real fear. Respondents specifically named financial scams and fake listings.
Roommate trust is a recurring issue. No trustworthy roommates and poor communication came up repeatedly.
Affordability decides everything. Budget had to be a primary filter, not an afterthought.

Compatibility criteria were consistent: cleanliness, gender, budget, lifestyle habits, noise level, safety, personality and location, with religion and work or study schedule also mattering to many, particularly outside Lagos.

quotes.quote: Honestly I've been on the hunt for a house for the past two months. The agent fee is too high.
A reliable app to find accommodation easily.
Eliminate or limit agency fees, including inspection fees.

blocks.heading: What this meant for the design
items: Simplify housing and roommate discovery into one connected experience.
Make compatibility information accessible during discovery, not after commitment.
Introduce trust-building elements that help users make informed decisions before they message.
Make budget and location primary filters rather than settings buried in a form.

paragraphs: We compared Bunkie with Roomies.com, Roomi, Facebook Marketplace, SpareRoom and WhatsApp groups across roommate matching, in-app messaging, identity verification, lifestyle filters and mobile availability. Most competitors offered limited or no structured lifestyle matching, and several had no real identity verification.

cards.title: Roomies.com
cards.body: Roommate profiles and a familiar search model, but lifestyle matching is shallow and verification is not the centre of the experience.

cards.title: Roomi
cards.body: Combines rooms and roommates in one app, but the trust layer is thin for a decision this personal.

cards.title: Facebook Marketplace
cards.body: Huge reach and a familiar posting flow, with no structured matching, verification or safe handoff into a conversation.

cards.title: SpareRoom
cards.body: Strong listing filters and room search, weaker lifestyle compatibility, and not built around the Nigerian market.

cards.title: WhatsApp groups
cards.body: Where people already search, but there is no search, no verification and no record of who is real.

callout.label: The opportunity
callout.text: Combine full lifestyle compatibility, integrated identity verification, and in-app messaging with a booking flow in a mobile-first product built for markets where phones, not desktops, are the main device.

sections.title: Defining the Product
sections.intro: Research shaped our scope. Bunkie has two core functions: find a roommate for people with an existing apartment, and find shared accommodation for people looking for a place.

blocks.heading: Version 1.0 features
items: Onboarding and profiles with email, Google or Apple sign-up, and a profile that must reach 70% completion before appearing in search.
Lifestyle questionnaire covering schedule, cleanliness, noise, pets, smoking, guests, religion, gender preference and budget.
Smart compatibility matching with a ranked list of matches, plus like, skip and save.
Housing and roommate listings with photos, price, location and listers' roommate preferences.
Search and filters by price, location, room type and lifestyle, with real-time results.
In-app messaging unlocked by mutual match, with report and block tools.
Identity verification via government ID and selfie check, shown as a verified badge.
Booking request flow between seeker and lister.

blocks.heading: Deliberately out of scope for V1
items: Payments
Tenancy agreements
Background checks
A landlord portal
External property integrations

callout.label: Why we cut them
callout.text: Keeping payments, leases and integrations out of V1 let us focus on the trust and matching problems users cared about most.

blocks.heading: Success targets
blocks.intro: Targets defined for the first three months after launch.

stats.label: Verified accounts

stats.description: Profiles completed past the visibility threshold

cards.title: Mobile-first
cards.body: Every screen is designed for a 375px width minimum, with desktop as a secondary experience.

cards.title: Progressive disclosure
cards.body: Show only what matters for the current task so new users are not overwhelmed.

cards.title: Trustworthy aesthetic
cards.body: A clean, minimal language that signals safety and reliability at every step.

sections.title: User Flows & Information Architecture
sections.intro: We mapped three key journeys before any wireframing, and used them to sequence the work across UX, UI, brand and product.

cards.title: Onboarding
cards.body: Splash, registration, OTP email verification, profile, lifestyle questionnaire, optional ID upload, personalised dashboard.

cards.title: Roommate matching
cards.body: Browse ranked suggestions, view a full profile, like or skip, mutual like triggers a match, then chat.

cards.title: Housing search and booking
cards.body: Search or map view, apply filters, view listing, save or request booking, lister accepts or declines, chat opens on acceptance.

blocks.heading: Navigation model
items: Discover: the shared entry point for rooms and roommates.
Saved: a shortlist of listings and profiles.
Create: the lister's entry point into the create-listing flow.
Inbox: conversations unlocked by a match or an accepted request.
Profile: identity, lifestyle preferences, listings, requests, FAQ and settings.

sections.title: Brand Identity
sections.intro: The Bunkie brand needed to feel warm and friendly, but also dependable, because users are being asked to trust strangers with their homes.

paragraphs: Purple carries trust, orange brings energy and action, and Manrope keeps the interface clear on small screens. The type scale starts at 32px headings and 16px body text.

The wordmark integrates a keyhole into the dot of the n, a small detail that signals access, privacy and housing discovery. It is subtle enough to feel like a mark rather than an illustration, and memorable enough to survive an app icon.

images.label: The keyhole inside the n represents access, privacy and housing discovery.
Wordmark and keyhole pattern applied across brand touchpoints.

paragraphs: Before high-fidelity screens, we built a design system covering buttons, cards, forms, icons and spacing rules so every screen stayed consistent and handoff to developers would be smooth.

cards.title: Foundations
cards.body: Colour roles, type scale, spacing, radii and elevation, shared by product and brand.

cards.title: Components
cards.body: Buttons, inputs, listing cards, profile cards, tags, filters and the bottom navigation.

cards.title: Patterns
cards.body: Verification prompts, empty states, bottom sheets, booking requests and listing lifecycle actions.

callout.label: Why it mattered
callout.text: A shared system let UI and brand work in parallel without drifting, and gave the development team one set of rules instead of four interpretations.

sections.title: Key Screens
sections.intro: We moved from low-fidelity wireframes based on the flows into high-fidelity screens that applied the design system. The screens below follow the journey from first launch to a published listing.

blocks.heading: Onboarding and lifestyle questionnaire
blocks.intro: A short questionnaire, kept to a maximum of eight questions with the benefit of better matches explained up front, to reduce drop-off. The prompt appears after the selfie check so the value is visible in context.

blocks.heading: Profile and verification
blocks.intro: Profiles show the compatibility information roommates need, along with a verified badge once ID verification is complete. Verification gates messaging, saving and listing, and the gate explains exactly what is checked and what stays private.

blocks.heading: Roommate and housing discovery
blocks.intro: One search surface for rooms and roommates, with a clear compatibility signal and simple like, skip and save actions. Saved listings and empty states keep the shortlist usable before it fills up.

screens.alt: Bunkie discover screen with rooms and roommates tabs
screens.label: Discover

blocks.heading: Housing, requests and listing creation
blocks.intro: Seekers can save a room or send a booking request. Listers get a guided four-step creation flow, with photo upload, description, amenities and a verification step before publishing.

sections.title: How We Worked
sections.intro: Four teams ran in parallel across eight weeks, with weekly Friday syncs, ClickUp for task tracking, WhatsApp for quick updates and a shared Google Doc as the official record.

cards.title: What I'm proud of
cards.body: Grounding every feature in survey evidence, from the 99% prior search rate to the frustration with agent and inspection fees.

cards.title: The challenge
cards.body: Sequencing work across four teams with strong dependencies, while balancing a rich questionnaire against onboarding drop-off.

cards.title: What I learned
cards.body: Trust is a product surface. Verification, reporting and the tone of a listing card do as much work as the matching algorithm.

blocks.heading: Next steps
items: Integrated rent payments and bill splitting.
In-app lease agreements with e-signing.
AI-powered compatibility scoring.
Landlord tools and a verified lister programme.
Community housing guides and neighbourhood reviews.

callout.label: Closing thought
callout.text: A home is not a listing. It is a person you can trust.
